request: Please find me data regarding first-of-class ship cost overruns

reply.reply:
**CRS reports estimate Columbia’s first ship at $16.1 billion (2024 dollars), give Ford’s first ship final procurement cost as $13,316.5 million, and show Columbia’s 12-ship procurement estimate rose 15.2% from FY2021 to FY2025.**

- The lead ship estimate is $1,499.3 million, higher than follow-on ships because it is at the top of the production learning curve and its procurement cost includes much of the class’s detailed design/nonrecurring engineering costs. (R44972, PDF p. 10)
- The Navy estimates the first Columbia-class ship will cost $16.1 billion in 2024 dollars, with construction complete in 2029. (R41129, PDF p. 16)
- The estimated total procurement cost for the 12-ship Columbia class increased 15.2% from the FY2021 budget estimate to the FY2025 estimate. (R41129, PDF p. 15)
- The ship’s final procurement cost was $13,316.5 million in then-year dollars. (RS20643, PDF p. 7)
reply.reasoning: CRS reports provide first-ship cost examples and explicit Columbia-class-wide estimate growth. The evidence does not support calculating an individual lead-ship overrun against its original baseline.
